qt: to the Commission Alberico Gambino (ECR), Alessandro Ciriani (ECR), Michele Picaro (ECR), Daniele Polato (ECR), Sergio Berlato (ECR), Francesco Torselli (ECR), Mariateresa Vivaldini (ECR), Stefano Cavedagna (ECR), Denis Nesci (ECR), Paolo Inselvini (ECR), Carlo Ciccioli (ECR), Pietro Fiocchi (ECR), Marco Squarta (ECR), Chiara Gemma (ECR), Nicola Procaccini (ECR), Francesco Ventola (ECR), Mario Mantovani (ECR) Subject:

The surge in fuel prices is bringing road transport to its knees, stifling businesses and threatening the economic and social resilience of Europe as a whole. The recent wave of road haulier protests in Italy is proof that this crisis – which has hit southern Italy particularly hard – is international in nature and threatens the very foundations of the European economy. The Meloni Government has already implemented extraordinary measures and continues in its efforts to protect families and businesses. That said, the right to strike cannot become a coercive instrument, and must co-exist with an equally sacrosanct principle: the right to work in an environment that is free of intimidation or restrictions. At a time of unprecedented international tension, Europe cannot hope to address the economic issues that these conflicts have thrown up with ordinary peacetime tools. We therefore ask the Commission: 1.
Will it urgently mobilise extraordinary European resources to support the hauliers, businesses and families who are struggling to cope with these high prices?

Does it agree that it should propose activating the safeguard clauses under the economic governance framework, thereby granting Member States the budgetary flexibility they need to deal with this emergency?
What immediate steps is it thinking of taking in order to ensure that supply chains are not brought to a halt and to safeguard the EU’s competitiveness and economic stability?
